correctness.rationale: All four finite graphs have been reconstructed and their perfect matchings exhaustively enumerated as graph-theoretic edge-subsets. The hexagonal prism has exactly 20 matchings, face vector (1,18,117,138,0), and a 16-leaf consistent depth-4 tree. The certificate was replayed independently of its generator. Four shattered edges are structurally ruled out: only rungs have frequency at least eight, and every four-rung support has a forcing contradiction. Since 20<32 no depth-5 tree exists.

value.rationale: An exact, motivated finite connectivity boundary: the smallest cycle prism with a strict adaptive advantage is a three-connected, cubic, planar, bipartite and matching-covered graph on twelve vertices. Earlier matching-query gap constructions use bridge-connected blocks or degree-two ladder corners. The explicit small witness and structural obstruction separate online from static complexity under stronger graph constraints. This is a natural cutoff, not a generic recomputation of one arbitrary graph statistic.
